concepts.why: Secular scholar / Jewish reader of the Hebrew Bible: the name is 'I will show My holiness', and Hab 1:13 says God's eyes are too pure to look on evil and then is the prophet's complaint about why God tolerates the faithless; it does not say God shows His holiness by judging. The other four verses (Lev 10:3, Isa 5:16, Ezek 28:22, Ezek 38:23) all say it. Dropping leaves 4 passages. Do not move it to 'Why does the way of the wicked prosper?', which is full at 8 and already has Hab 1:4.

note_fixes: Ezekiel 18:2: the note quotes only the proverb ('The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge'), which is the saying the LORD is asking the people to stop quoting. Standing alone under this name it reads as the concept's claim. Quote the whole sentence of the verse, 'What do you people mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: ...?', so the note is the question, not the proverb.
concepts.why: Reformed / Orthodox / Catholic readers (who hold a corporate or inherited side to guilt) and the secular scholar: a note that quotes the refuted proverb alone can be taken as what the text affirms. Nothing else in the concept needs changing; Exod 20:5 standing in 'A jealous God' beside it is the right way to leave the two.

Secular scholar: Luke 8:17 sits in the lamp saying, about the word being made known; nothing in the verse or its setting is a judgment, and Luke 12:3 says the same thing in a setting of fear and accounting. The concept is 'every hidden thing brought to light' in judgment, so the verse that shares the words but not the matter goes. Seven passages remain.

Same sub-theme as 29 (see the duplicates entry below). Zeph 1:14-15, which sits under 29, begins 'The great Day of the LORD is near' and goes on 'That day will be a day of wrath': the text itself puts the two names on one day. Recommend merging 29 into this concept (keep the name 'The Day of the LORD'), trimmed to 8 by dropping the repeats: Ezek 30:3, Joel 1:15 and Mal 4:5 here, and Prov 11:4 and Lam 2:22 from 29. The merged concept would hold Isa 2:12, Isa 13:9, Joel 2:11, Amos 5:18, Zeph 1:14-15, Ezek 7:19, Rom 2:5, Rev 6:16-17 (1 Thess 5:2 is the ninth; drop whichever the owner prefers). Setting Rom 2:5 and Rev 6:16-17 under the name is not a claim that they name the same day as the Old Testament texts any more than the outline claims it now, since 'day of wrath' is listed in the same table row as the Day of the LORD.

Duplicate of 27: merge into it (see 27 and the duplicates entry). If the owner keeps the two apart, they need a difference a reader can see; as it stands the same verse (Zeph 1:14-15) says both names.

concepts.name: Those who will judge
concepts.why: Baptist / dispensational reader, Reformed and Catholic readers, and the secular scholar on Israel and the church: the name 'The saints will judge the world' is 1 Cor 6:2, but Matt 19:28 and Luke 22:30 say the Twelve will judge 'the twelve tribes of Israel', not the world. Under that name the grouping says that the Twelve are 'the saints' and that Israel is 'the world', which is the Israel-and-church question settled by the heading. A plain label ('Those who will judge', or 'Judging with thrones') names what the four passages share and leaves each object as the text has it. The notes and passages are unchanged. Dan 7:22 and Rev 20:4 stay out for the reasons the drafter gave.

Matt 12:36 says 'the day of judgment' in so many words, which is the name of concept 36, and the two concepts are otherwise close (see duplicates). Move Matt 12:36 to 36 (it then has 7); this leaves 37 about standing and giving account (Rom 14:10, 12; 2 Cor 5:10; Heb 9:27; Eccl 11:9) and gives each a verse that carries its own name. Baptist / dispensational reader: the name 'We will all stand' is Rom 14:10's and does not say the judgment seat of Christ and God's seat are one event or two, which should stay so.

concepts.name: I do not know you
concepts.why: Name against passages: Matt 25:11-12 does not say 'Depart from Me'; the master says 'I do not know you'. Only Matt 7:23 and Luke 13:27 say depart. The phrase all three share is the not-knowing (Matt 7:23 'I never knew you'; Matt 25:12 'I do not know you'; Luke 13:25, 27 'I do not know where you are from'). 'I do not know you' is Matt 25:12's words and does not decide, as 'I never knew you' might to a Reformed or Wesleyan reader, whether they were once known. 'Depart from Me, you who are cursed' (Matt 25:41) already stands in 'The sheep and the goats'.

Name against passage: 'Eternal fire' is said by Matt 18:8 and Jude 7, 'unquenchable'/'never quenched' by Isa 66:24 and Mark 9:43, 48, and Rev 14:10-11 has 'forever and ever'; Matt 5:22 says only 'the fire of hell' and the verse is about calling a brother a fool, so it is longer than the concept needs and does not say what the name says. Six passages remain, and the conditionalist and traditional readings of the other words still both have their texts in 45, 47, 49.

Name against passages: Rev 2:11 says 'the second death' and does not mention the lake of fire; the equation is made by 20:14 and 21:8, which stay. Four passages remain. Rev 19:20 and 20:10 are the lake without the words second death, so the shorter name 'The lake of fire' is the one that fits them all.

note_fixes: Job 21:18 (if kept instead of dropped): extend the passage to 21:17-18 so Job's 'How often...' question that precedes it is in the passage, and quote the question whole.
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Jewish reader of Job: Job 21:18 alone, 'Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?', is a rhetorical question whose answer in Job's mouth is no. In an outline whose chaff concept (44) says the opposite, the bare line reads as a statement. Either drop it (the concept has 8 passages without a gap) or give the whole question with 21:17 so the denial is in front of the reader.

secondary_or_links: Duplicates (same sub-theme named twice): 27 'The Day of the LORD' and 29 'The day of wrath'. Zeph 1:14-15 (now under 29) opens 'The great Day of the LORD' and says 'That day will be a day of wrath'; Isa 13:9 under 27 describes it with 'fury and burning anger'. The drafter's reason for keeping them apart (that Rom 2:5 and Rev 6:16-17 would then sit under the name 'The Day of the LORD') is answered by the merged concept being titled by the table's own row and leaving each verse's words as written; the 8-passage ceiling is met by the trims listed under 27. A second, closer-than-comfortable pair is 36 'The day of judgment' and 37 'We will all stand before God's judgment seat', held apart only by moving Matt 12:36 to 36 as listed under 37; no merge advised for these.

Last concept: 62 'In Your wrath, remember mercy' is the theme's own words of hope (Hab 3:2, Ps 30:5, Isa 12:1, Isa 54:7-8, Lam 3:31-32, Mic 7:9, 7:18, Jas 2:13), every passage inside the theme, with the anger kept in the notes (Isa 54:7-8 'surge of anger', Mic 7:9 'the rage of the LORD', Jas 2:13 'judgment without mercy'). Nothing dark is left out of the run before it: the curses, hidden face, wrath, winepress, the day of wrath, eternal fire, the lake of fire, weeping and gnashing, and 'perish' are each their own concept. Accept as it stands; do not add a closing line saying the texts end in hope.

Where traditions part (last things, hell): the texts are side by side and I would not reorder or rename. 'Eternal fire', 'The lake of fire', 'Weeping and gnashing of teeth' (forever and ever, never quenched, eternal punishment in 41:46) stand beside 'The way of the wicked will perish', 'Like chaff', Mal 4:1, Matt 10:28 and 2 Thess 1:9 (perish, destroy, eternal destruction), and no heading says which is right. Rev 20:4-6 is left out and Rev 20:11-15 is cut to 12-15, which keeps the order of the last things undecided. Order 31-46 reads as no sequence a reader could defend as one tradition's scheme; leave it.
Concept 33 (1 Thess 3:13 'with all His saints' beside Zech 14:5 'all the holy ones'): the name uses both 'angels' and 'holy ones', so it does not say who comes with Him; leave the notes as quoted.

Secondary concepts: all ten stand. 'Judgment -> The sword' and 'Wrath -> The cup' are in the texts' words; 'Exile -> Gathered back, a new heart' (Ezek 36:24, 26) puts the Old Testament promise beside nothing from the New, which is right.

Links: ten is enough; with the limit lifted no further link is needed for completeness. 'Temple/Presence' could be re-added for Lev 10:2-3, Ezek 9:6 and the hidden face, but the drafter's reason (overlap only in passing) is fair.

missing.sub_theme: Because of the wickedness of these nations
missing.why: The driving out of the nations before Israel is stated by the Torah itself as the LORD's judgment on them ('it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is driving them out', Deut 9:4-5; 'the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete', Gen 15:16; 'the land vomited out its inhabitants', Lev 18:25) and is the hardest dark strand of the theme. The outline has judgment on the flood, Sodom, Egypt, Babylon and Israel but none on the peoples of the land; leaving it out reads as softening. Deut 9:3 already stands in 'A consuming fire'.

Judgment as the LORD letting people have what they chose ('So I gave them over to their stubborn hearts', Ps 81:12; 'God gave them over' three times in Rom 1:24-28; 'God turned away and gave them over', Acts 7:42) is plainly developed in the Psalms, the history and Paul, and is a kind of judgment none of the 62 concepts names; 'I will hide My face' (10) is the nearest and is a different act. Hardening texts (Exod 4:21, Isa 6:9-10, Rom 9:18) are where traditions part and are best left out of this concept.
